newsitem.title: JAPAN: Walgreen to enter Japan drugstore deal. [CORRECTED 03:30 GMT 8/5]
newsitem.headline: Walgreen to enter Japan drugstore deal. [CORRECTED 03:30 GMT 8/5]

text.p: Walgreen Co, a leading U.S. drugstore operator, wil provide technical assistance to a drugstore joint venture set up by six Japanese companies to start a chain of stores in Japan, one of the partners to the project said on Wednesday.

Convenience chain store operator FamilyMart Co Ltd said it together with five other Japanese firms -- Itochu Corp, Hac Kimisawa Co, Kraft Inc, CRC Research Institute Inc and Japan Leasing Corp -- had set up a venture capitalised at 250 million yen.

Walgreen has no initial ownership in the venture, but it has an option to purchase a share of the company in the future. (Corrects by clarifying throughout that Walgreen is providing technical assistance to, not joining, the Japanese venture.)
Itochu is currently the largest shareholder in the venture with a 37 percent interest, but Walgreen will become the top shareholder in two to three years, a FamilyMart spokesman said.
The new company, RX Network Inc, is expected to have 500 member drugstores in Japan by 2002, he added.

"The venture aims to offer better services to customers by managing data on their prescription and medical history through the help of an Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) system," the spokesman said.
An increasing number of Japanese hospitals are now prescribing drugs so that patients can buy them at drugstores.
In the past, most hospitals sold prescription medicine themselves.
